title: Short-lag gait volatility memory provides no robust incremental Parkinson prediction across two public datasets
abstract: Magnitude correlations can encode temporal organization not summarized by stride variability. We tested one fixed short-lag statistic against demographic, conventional gait, linear-dynamics and tail-shape predictors. Logistic models were trained on31 gaitndd participants and frozen for151 gaitpdb participants. Adding lag-two absolute stride-increment correlation changed external Brier score from 0.339803 to 0.339786 (delta -0.00001684; joint source/target bootstrap95% interval [-0.017444,+0.012658]). Target-only resampling gave a narrowly negative interval but source refitting removed this apparent precision. Source leave-one-out performance worsened. Both rich models transferred poorly (AUC about0.525). This exploratory, model-specific negative result does not establish equivalence, absence of nonlinear physiology, or clinical diagnostic utility; participant nonoverlap is not fully verifiable.
